title: Register changes after the corrected E01 static run, V2-S2-004-PR2
description: What V2-S2-004-PR2 changed in the register once the static parts of V2-E01 had run under freeze revision 2: every register change with its value before and after, the one correction it writes beside the first run's result page, and the findings each answers. It is the fourth ledger written after v1.0.0 was released, and like the three before it, it is not part of the pack that release was cut over: the evidence index undoes it, with the other post-release ledgers, to recompute that pack. It adds one claim, certified at C0 on the one record it adds with it, appends a dated audit limitation to the first run's claim, and moves no existing claim's status or record. It raises and closes no blocker, declares no freeze, states no release, and edits no dated record.

claim.statement: The committed evidence of the second run of the frozen E01 static parts, the first under freeze revision 2, records that the runner and the inferops package were imported from the merged checkout it executed and that every repository module file it loaded was a pinned input, and holds two renders of the V1 synchronous reference contract on its local binding, written by two processes, that are byte-identical and record their sources; no hand-written string that contains a generated workload-intent value; a render after a replica-range change that differs only in the values and release fields that change owns; and, for each of seven registered invalid or conflicting inputs, two identical refusals that match the registered one and no output directory.
claim.limitation: Static, C0, about the committed evidence of one run on one host at one revision, for one contract on one binding. The renderer that produced it is product code and ran; a claim about the renderer itself would be C2 and is not made. Nothing was deployed, reconciled, or served. The run answers freeze revision 2 only: it is not evidence that the first run, 20261002-e01-abc-1, executed under a valid execution boundary. One of the seven refusals, E01-C-4, comes from the binding parser and carries a code and a field but no rule category. The platform-defaults revision a release records is asserted, not reconstructed. The download URL and licence reference are derived from the contract's pins, and nothing fetches either. The import closure the freeze pins is static, and the interpreter, the standard library, and third-party packages are not pinned by content.
claim.doesNotEstablish: That the release input deploys or serves, which E01-D owns and has not run; that the first run's execution was governed by its freeze; that the renderer gives the same result at another revision, or for another workload shape, contract, or binding; that either derived URL resolves; that any invalid input beyond the seven registered cases is refused; reliability under failure; or production readiness.

evidenceRecords.summary: On 2026-10-03 the static parts of V2-E01 ran once, as freeze revision 2 registers them, at the merged revision a5b6a5db2011a68a3f27acdeaa8186c226bfedb4 with the record registered and unedited, no material file changed, absent, added, or out of scope, and nothing uncommitted before the run; the runner and the inferops package were imported from that checkout; E01-A, E01-B, and E01-C each PASSED, and python -m tools.experiment_e01 --check judges the committed run again from its renders, its refusals, and the observations its manifest records.

executedComponents.note: tools/experiment_e01, imported from the checked-out tree at the executing revision, where every file of it is a pinned input of freeze revision 2; it parsed the pinned inputs and called the render package's generate_release, write_release, and admit_manual_values in process. The run manifest records each runner file's digest and every repository module file both processes loaded.

src/inferops/domain/render at the executing revision, the product code that wrote the renders and raised the refusals this record inspects; it is a tool here because the claim is about the committed evidence it produced, not about the renderer at any other revision.

tools/experiment_freeze, called by the runner before any part: the freeze record is registered and equals its registered pin, and no file in the record's material scope is changed, absent, added, or out of scope.

python -m tools.experiment_e01 --check, deriving every verdict again from the committed renders, the recorded refusals, and the observations the manifest records, and comparing it with the recorded outcomes, file digests, and result page; it does not recompute the contract, binding, or mutated-contract digests, the admission, the restated-value search, or the V1 merge.

workload.description: No workload was issued. The inputs were the pinned contract, binding, chart defaults, hand-written values, and V1 values, read as files, with the edits the freeze record registers.

environment.note: One Windows host, version 10.0.26200, Python 3.12.12 under uv 0.9.16 (a63e5b62e 2025-12-06), in a checkout at the executing revision with no change before the run and only the run's evidence directory after it, on 2026-10-03; the parts contacted no cluster, network, runtime, or model.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The two renders are canonically identical: both files are byte-identical, the SHA-256 of each file is equal, and metadata.releaseId is equal.
The release records the source contract digest, and it equals contract_digest of the parsed contract.
The release records the EnvironmentBinding's name, apiVersion, and digest, and they equal local-kind, inferops.io/v1alpha1, and binding_digest of the parsed binding.

The release records the generated values digest, and it equals the SHA-256 of the bytes of the values file beside it. The renderer and platform-defaults revisions it records equal the executing commit.

No claim-relevant workload intent is written by hand after rendering: admit_manual_values admits the hand-written values with no finding; every chart value that a workload-intent context value renders to, or that is derived from workload-intent context values only, is in the generated values file; no hand-written string contains one of those generated values of eight characters or more; and the generated and hand-written values, merged over the chart's defaults, equal the V1 real values merged the same way, except telemetry.deploymentEnvironment, which is local in V2 and dev in V1 as the V1 synchronous compatibility record states.

The mutation changes only the expected semantic output: in values.generated.yaml, only runtime.replicaCount, from 1 to 2; in rendered-workload-release.yaml, only metadata.releaseId, output.helmValues.sha256, and source.contract.sha256; and source.contract.sha256 equals contract_digest of the mutated contract.

Every negative case is refused at its registered step with its expected refusal: for a RenderRefused, exactly the registered findings, in order, each with its rule, category, code, and field; for E01-C-4, the registered exception type, code, and field. No case writes an output directory, and each case's second execution gives the same refusal as its first.

results.statement: render-a and render-b, written by two processes with PYTHONHASHSEED 1 and 2, are byte-identical in both files, and both releases carry the same metadata.releaseId.
The render-a release records the source contract digest, and it equals contract_digest of the parsed contract.
The render-a release records the binding as local-kind, inferops.io/v1alpha1, with the digest binding_digest gives for the parsed binding.
The render-a release records the SHA-256 of the values file beside it, and the executing revision as both its renderer and its platform-defaults revision.

admit_manual_values admitted the hand-written values with no finding, all 22 workload-intent chart values, the two derived model references among them, are in the generated file, no hand-written string contains one of those generated values of eight characters or more, and the two merged value sets differ only at telemetry.deploymentEnvironment, local in V2 and dev in V1.

Setting the replica range to two moved runtime.replicaCount from 1 to 2 and no other value, and moved only metadata.releaseId, output.helmValues.sha256, and source.contract.sha256 in the release, the last equal to contract_digest of the mutated contract.

Each of the seven negative cases was refused at its registered step with exactly its registered refusal, six with a rule, a category, and a code and E01-C-4 by the binding parser with a code and a field, left its output directory absent, and was refused the same way when run a second time.

limitations: One run on one Windows host at one revision, with one contract on one binding.
The renderer ran as a tool and its release input was inspected; the release input was not deployed, reconciled, or served.

The platform-defaults revision a release records is asserted, not reconstructed. The download URL and licence reference are derived from the contract's pins by one rule for one model source, and nothing fetches either.

The freeze pins the static import closure of the runner's entry module and the data files the parts read. The run recorded 47 repository module files loaded by its first process and 47 by its second, each a pinned input with its pinned content. The Python interpreter, the standard library, and third-party packages are not pinned by content; uv.lock pins the third-party versions.
This is the first run under freeze revision 2. It answers revision 2's criteria only, and it is not evidence that the first run, 20261002-e01-abc-1, executed under a valid execution boundary.
The rule against previews is a procedure, and no code enforces it. The validation record states what executed before the run.

The renderer that produced the evidence is product code in src/, and it executed. The record is C0 because the claim is about the committed evidence and the freeze record registers C0 for these parts; a claim that the renderer renders deterministically at any revision would, by the register's parser row, be C2, and is not made.

The --check judge derives verdicts from the committed renders and refusals and from observations the run recorded; the contract, binding, and mutated-contract digests, the admission, the restated-value search, and the V1 merge are the run's observations, not recomputed.
doesNotEstablish: That the release input deploys through Git and Argo CD or serves a completion: E01-D owns that and has not run.
That the first run's execution was governed by its freeze.
That another workload shape, contract, or binding renders deterministically.
That the renderer gives the same result at any revision other than the one that ran.
That the derived download URL or licence reference resolves.
That any invalid input beyond the seven registered cases is refused.
Reliability under failure, or production readiness.

registerChanges.reason: The static parts of V2-E01 ran once under the merged freeze revision 2, from the merged checkout, and every criterion held. The register states what the run's committed evidence shows, at C0, in a claim of its own, so the first run's claim and record stay as they were recorded. The claim is appended to the register, so no existing pointer into it moves. Its status follows the decision the maintainer made for the first run's claim.

recordCorrections.correction: Dated 2026-10-03. The preconditions the run checked were the ones freeze revision 1 stated, and each held as recorded. The audit of the first Sprint 2 collective review found that they did not govern the run's execution boundary: the runner the run executed was not in the commit the run records and was not a pinned input of revision 1, so revision 1's change check could not report it, and the location of the imported inferops package was observed by hand and not recorded by the run. Full executions of the parts in throwaway repositories, one before the run and two after it, were not registered beforehand, and their raw evidence is not available. The run is not evidence that its execution was governed by its freeze. The page, the run's other files, their digests, and the revision 1 outcomes are unchanged, and the run is still judged by revision 1. The runner digests the run recorded are of the runner before its independent review changed it, so the runner files committed beside the run are not the ones that ran.

findings.observation: E01-A, E01-B, and E01-C ran once under freeze revision 2, at the merged revision, with the runner and the inferops package imported from that checkout, and each PASSED. The one E01 claim in the register is about the first run, under revision 1, and its record cites that run only.
findings.resolution: A new claim states the second run's result at C0 and holds its record. The first run's claim keeps its statement, status, and record. The planned deployment claim is unchanged; E01-D, which deploys and serves, is the run that could show it.

findings.observation: The first Sprint 2 collective review, on 2026-10-03, found that the first run executed a runner outside its executing revision and outside freeze revision 1's pins, and that full previews were not registered beforehand. Freeze revision 2 and the experiments page record that audit limitation. The first run's claim, and the result page its record cites, did not.
findings.resolution: The dated audit limitation is appended to the claim's limitation, and one correction is written beside the first run's result page. The page, the run, the record, and the claim's status are unchanged.
